cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Change What the Apology Is For
cards.instruction: Get an apology, then reveal that the original offense was only the first layer of what needs repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you for admitting you broke the vase. I pointed at the dog just as firmly as you did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was pointing him away from the glass, not saying he broke it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, keeping him clear. Now apologize for letting me spend three days calling him destructive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry. I'll take him for a long walk to make it up to him.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me you should have corrected me before you take him. He gets the walk; I need that sentence.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copied pointing borrows blame; B2 reveals safety direction, A3 saves face and expands the apology to uncorrected scolding; A5 distinguishes B4 compensation for dog from acknowledgment owed to A.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 glass correction causes A3 three-day omission demand; B4 walk offer causes A5 separate verbal repair request.

relationship.evidence: B4 apologizes and proposes a real kindness to the dog, giving A a plausible partial solution to redirect.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 dog-focused repair to expose A's remaining need without inventing a new offense.

specificity.evidence: A1 broken vase/dog, B2 glass and A3 three days establish the misunderstanding and its persistence.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 he gets walk/I need sentence is concise, pointed division of two actual repairs.
